question: What is the main goal of palliative care in cancer treatment?
explanation: Palliative care focuses on relieving distress and enhancing the quality of life rather than curing the disease. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why are systemic cancer therapies used instead of localized treatments when cancer has spread?

options.A: They act exclusively on localized solid tumors
options.B: They avoid all forms of systemic toxicity and adverse effects
options.C: They replace the need for surgical staging completely
options.D: They travel via the bloodstream to reach widespread malignant cells

explanation: Systemic medications circulate through the blood vessels, allowing them to reach cancer cells that have spread to different parts of the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which waste container is used for discarded chemotherapy materials?
explanation: Special yellow containers are used for the safe disposal and incineration of hazardous cytotoxic waste. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h2)

question: A nurse spills an intravenous chemotherapy drug inside the safety cabinet. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Spray regular hospital disinfectant over the affected surface
options.B: Leave the hood running and wait for the maintenance team
options.C: Wipe the surface immediately with a standard dry paper towel
options.D: Use the designated chemotherapy spill kit to clean the area

explanation: Certified spill kits contain neutralizing agents and materials designed specifically to clean up hazardous drug spills safely. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h2)

question: How do targeted cancer therapies differ from traditional chemotherapy?

options.A: They focus on specific molecular features driving cancer cell growth
options.B: They require continuous infusion pumps rather than oral dosing
options.C: They work exclusively by boosting the patient's white blood cells
options.D: They destroy all rapidly dividing cells throughout the entire body

explanation: Targeted drugs zero in on precise proteins or genetic changes unique to cancer cells, unlike traditional chemotherapy which affects all fast-growing cells. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the main action of immune checkpoint inhibitors in cancer care?

options.A: Inhibiting the hormonal production of estrogen in female patients
options.B: Emitting localized ionizing radiation to shrink tumor blood vessels
options.C: Blocking proteins that prevent T-cells from attacking cancer cells
options.D: Directly replacing damaged bone marrow stem cells with donors

explanation: Checkpoint inhibitors remove the signals that hold back the immune system, allowing T-cells to attack the tumor. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which type of cancer is most commonly treated with hormone therapy?

options.D: Small cell carcinoma of the lung

explanation: Hormones like estrogen can fuel certain breast cancers, so blocking these hormones is an effective treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the main goal of hormone therapy in cancer treatment?

options.A: Enhance the replication rate of healthy endocrine glands
options.B: Lower hormone production or block receptors feeding the tumor
options.C: Replace damaged cellular DNA within the bone marrow
options.D: Stimulate systemic inflammatory responses against metastasis

explanation: Depriving hormone-dependent cancers of their growth signals helps slow or stop the disease from progressing. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why are ink marks placed on the skin before external beam radiation therapy?

options.A: Guiding the surgeon during subsequent resections
options.B: Identifying areas of active bacterial skin infection
options.C: Mapping out sites for intravenous cannula insertion
options.D: Ensuring precise daily targeting of the tumor site

explanation: Skin markings ensure the radiation beam is directed to the exact same spot during every treatment session. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h5)

question: A patient receiving radiation to the neck asks if they can use scented lotion on the area. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Avoid perfumed lotions because they can irritate the sensitive skin
options.B: Rub the scented cream vigorously to enhance skin absorption
options.C: Use alcohol-based rubs instead to keep the skin sterile and dry
options.D: Apply the lotion heavily right before each radiation session begins

explanation: Fragrances and chemicals can worsen skin irritation and breakdown within the radiation treatment field. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the most reliable early sign of infection in a patient with neutropenia?
explanation: Because neutropenic patients have low white blood cells and may not show typical signs like pus or swelling, fever is often the only warning sign of infection. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why is mouth care so important for a patient undergoing chemotherapy?

options.A: It prevents painful mucosal ulcerations and secondary infections
options.B: It stimulates the appetite by clearing leftover food debris
options.C: It maintains adequate salivary pH levels during dehydration
options.D: It stops systemic bone marrow suppression from worsening

explanation: Chemotherapy harms rapidly dividing cells in the mouth lining, making good oral hygiene vital to prevent severe sores and infection. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h6)

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is a classic sign of tumor lysis syndrome?
explanation: The rapid breakdown of cancer cells releases large amounts of potassium into the bloodstream, causing dangerous hyperkalemia. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is an early warning sign of spinal cord compression in a cancer patient?

options.A: Throbbing headaches worse in the early morning
options.B: Intermittent cramping abdominal pain after meals
options.C: New onset back pain accompanied by motor weakness
options.D: Sharp chest pain radiating down the left arm

explanation: Tumor pressure on the spinal cord usually starts with back pain, followed by nerve problems like muscle weakness or numbness. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h7)

question: What preventive care is standard for a patient starting regular opioid pain medication?

options.A: Monitoring hourly urine output via a catheter
options.B: Administering prescribed stool softeners and laxatives
options.C: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload
options.D: Checking deep tendon reflexes every four hours

explanation: Opioids slow down bowel movements, so starting a bowel routine early is essential to prevent severe constipation. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h8)

question: How does palliative care differ from curative treatment?

options.A: It is administered only after all chemotherapy regimens fail
options.B: It prioritizes comfort and symptom relief over disease eradication
options.C: It is restricted exclusively to the final 24 hours of life
options.D: It forbids the use of any medications that affect consciousness

explanation: Palliative care can be started at any point during a serious illness to ease suffering and improve quality of life, regardless of whether a cure is possible. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h8)
